name: Lupus erythematosus panniculitis

ethnicAssociations: More common in females of African and Asian descent

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, histopathological, and immunological findings

criteria.description: Presence of deep, firm, indurated subcutaneous nodules or plaques typically on face, upper arms, trunk, or buttocks
Biopsy showing lobular lymphocytic panniculitis with hyaline fat necrosis and lymphoid aggregates
Direct immunofluorescence demonstrating granular deposits of IgG, IgM, and/or C3 at dermoepidermal junction or around fat lobules
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) or other lupus-specific autoantibodies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation of panniculitis with supportive histopathological findings; immunofluorescence and serology supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of panniculitis such as infections, trauma, or other connective tissue diseases

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep subcutaneous indurated nodules or plaques
pathognomonic.notes: Typically painless or mildly tender, located on face, upper arms, trunk, or buttocks
Characteristic lobular panniculitis with lymphocytic infiltration
searchTerms: fat tissue necrosis with glassy appearance
hyaline fat cell death on biopsy
fat tissue damage with hyaline changes

common.notes: Redness of skin overlying panniculitis lesions
Depressed scars due to fat loss
May be positive in many patients

common.symptomName: Tenderness or mild pain at lesion sites

occasional.notes: Some patients may have concurrent SLE manifestations
Enlarged lymph nodes near lesion sites

laboratory: Possible anti-dsDNA or anti-Sm antibodies in some cases
Elevated ESR or CRP in systemic involvement
imaging: Ultrasound may show hypoechoic subcutaneous nodules
MRI can demonstrate lobular panniculitis with fat necrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; association with HLA-DR2 and HLA-DR3 alleles reported in lupus spectrum
other: Histopathology showing lobular lymphocytic panniculitis with hyaline fat necrosis
Direct immunofluorescence with granular IgG, IgM, and C3 deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of target lesions on skin
Histology shows interface dermatitis with epidermal necrosis
Usually associated with infections or drug reactions

redFlags: Development of systemic lupus erythematosus symptoms
Signs of secondary infection in skin lesions
references: Tuffanelli DL, Dubois EL. Lupus erythematosus panniculitis. Arch Dermatol. 1961;84:702-713.
Marzano AV, et al. Lupus erythematosus panniculitis: clinical and histopathologic study of 25 cases. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2003;48(2):263-270.
